title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Lumen Financial
summary: Walkthrough of Lumen's SIG/CAIQ and vendor risk questionnaire focused on SOC 2 scope, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, data residency, and encryption/KMS evidence. SE clarified architecture and evidence artifacts; action items: send SOC2 report, provide diagram of VPC/private deployment options, and export sample audit logs/masked. Next steps agreed: deliver docs and schedule follow-up in one week to review evidence.
action_items: Jordan - Send latest SOC 2 Type II report and cover letter - due 2026-06-20
Maya - Share VPC/private deployment diagram and network boundary doc - due 2026-06-22
Maya - Provide sample masked audit log export and retention policy excerpt - due 2026-06-22
Jordan - Share SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet export and list of evidence attachments - due 2026-06-20
next_steps: Redwood to upload SOC2 and SIG export to shared secure link
Schedule follow-up call to review evidence and open items (target 2026-06-25)
Customer to identify any additional stakeholders for legal/compliance review
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (Lumen CISO), Priya Anand (Lumen Head IT Ops), Evan Moore (Lumen Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, i'm Jordan with Redwood Inference, AE on the account. with me is Maya, our security and architecture lead.
[00:12] Maya: hi all, thanks. i'll be walking through the SIG and the typical evidence artifacts we can provide.
[00:20] Carlos: great, thanks. high level we're doing vendor risk for our platform team. primary concerns are SOC 2 scope, data residency for eu customers, and encryption key control. also need to see audit logs.
[00:32] Jordan: understood. we got your questionnaire in advance — we prioritized the SIG CAIQ sections you flagged. we'll go section by section and call out what we can provide as artifacts.
[00:45] Maya: quick note — transcription may pick up some names oddly, so if i say KV cache or K B cache that might be auto not perfect.
[00:52] Priya: hah, heard that before.
[00:54] Maya: okay starting with compliance posture — SOC 2. Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II, report available for customers under an NDA. our SOC scope currently covers the hosted API and dedicated control plane; private on-prem offering is outside the SOC boundary but we provide guidance and attestation steps.
[01:20] Carlos: is iso27001 in scope? we have a mandate to prioritize vendors with ISO or equivalent.
[01:26] Maya: we don't currently hold ISO 27001 cert; it's on the roadmap. we provide compensating controls and third-party risk docs; we can highlight our policies and timelines in the evidence package.
[01:38] Evan: procurement note — if iso is required we might need a timeline for when it will be achieved. can you provide a projected date?
[01:45] Jordan: we can provide a formal milestone doc. i'll follow up with product on an expected window but can't commit here on the call.
[01:53] Maya: moving to identity. we support SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC for our console and role-based access control. we expose fine-grained RBAC for routes and model access. for enterprise we integrate with SCIM for user provisioning.
[02:10] Priya: can we map roles to our internal AD groups?
[02:14] Maya: yes, SCIM + group mapping is supported. we can share a sample mapping we use for other finance customers.
[02:22] Carlos: audit logging — what events do you capture and how long are they retained?
[02:26] Maya: we capture admin logins, API request metadata (route, model id, response status), policy changes, and admin actions like user role changes. default retention in hosted is 90 days in the standard plan, with add-on for 365 days. dedicated/private options have configurable retention. we can provide a sample masked export.
[02:48] Evan: about masking — for PII in logs do you redact at rest or before export?
[02:53] Maya: we redact sensitive payloads before storing logs in our analytics pipeline. payload-level data is not stored by default; for customers who enable request logging we provide masking options and an allowlist.
[03:06] Carlos: data residency — we need EU only for eu-customer traffic. do you have region pinning?
[03:10] Maya: yes, region pinning and routing policies exist. hosted EU regions keep data in eu zones; dedicated and private give you full control. we'll include a network diagram and routing policy doc.
[03:22] Priya: for private on-prem, how does the control plane talk to the data plane? we need to understand ingress/egress paths for audits.
[03:28] Maya: private deployments can be fully air-gapped; our control plane can be run in customer VPC or we support a customer-managed control plane. standard private setup uses mTLS between control and data plane and only outbound connections to our update endpoints. we'll attach the architecture diagram.
[03:47] Jordan: quick aside — we sometimes get questions about fallback to hosted models and cross-region calls. we have policies to ensure data residency is honored; fallback is region aware and customers can opt-out.
[03:58] Carlos: encryption specifics — at rest and in transit? where are keys managed?
[04:02] Maya: TLS v1.2+ in transit. at rest we use AES-256. for hosted we use customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) when customers enable CMEK; otherwise we use our managed keys. for private we support bring-your-own-key and HSM integrations. we'll include KMS configuration docs and sample IAM policies.
[04:26] Evan: do you provide proof of key rotation and key access logs?
[04:30] Maya: yes, key access and rotation events are logged — we can provide a set of audit events from KMS and include rotation schedule and process docs.
[04:38] Priya: on SIG/CAIQ specifics — can you walk through the evidence mapping? we need to know which questionnaire items map to which artifacts.
[04:46] Maya: absolutely. we maintain a SIG export with responses and attached evidence links. common attachments: SOC 2 report, architecture diagrams, encryption/KMS config snippets, SLA and support process, incident response plan, penetration test summary, and policy docs (access control, change management). we'll share the spreadsheet export and a PDF bundle.
[05:06] Carlos: what about penetration test reports — full reports or redacted?
[05:10] Maya: typically a redacted summary plus statements from our external pen tester; full reports are provided under NDA on a case-by-case basis.
[05:18] Jordan: noted — we'll include the pen test summary and note the NDA process.
[05:22] Maya: evidence delivery — we can provide a secure link (expiring) for artefacts. Our SOC2 is gated behind an NDA; SIG/CAIQ attachments that aren't sensitive we can share directly.
[05:34] Evan: on procurement timeline, if we get the evidence by next tuesday can legal finish review in two weeks?
[05:39] Jordan: sounds plausible. we'll aim to deliver SOC2 and SIG export by 2026-06-20 as action items.
[05:46] Priya: one last technical question — can you support VPC endpoints or private link for your hosted API?
[05:51] Maya: yes, we support private networking options including AWS PrivateLink and VPC endpoints for supported regions. dedicated customers often use those for egress controls. we'll include configuration examples.
[06:02] Carlos: ok great. any open security issues or recent incidents we should be aware of?
[06:06] Maya: no active incidents; we have post-mortem summaries for older incidents and a change log. we can include the incident response timeline and remediation actions.
[06:15] Jordan: to recap — we'll send SOC2 Type II, SIG/CAIQ export, architecture and VPC diagram, sample masked logs, KMS docs, and pen test summary. we'll put artifacts on a secure share and schedule a follow up for 2026-06-25 to go over any remaining questions.
[06:32] Carlos: that works. can you also include the SLA for dedicated and the commit lead times?
[06:37] Jordan: yes i'll include the dedicated SLA doc and capacity commit options.
[06:42] Evan: procurement will expect vendor risk questionnaire answers inline too — not just attachments. can you populate the questionnaire and return as a tracked-changes PDF?
[06:51] Jordan: we can fill the form and return both a populated PDF and a SIG export.
[06:56] Priya: perfect. thanks everyone.
[06:59] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the link and docs.
[07:02] END

Notes: transcript timestamps correspond to call progression not exact seconds; some lines represent short edits. Transcript contains occasional auto-transcription errors and shorthand.
